reason: Changing a previously established value requires an earlier state.
A conflict with a previous session requires a previous session containing the original fact.
An expired promotion must first exist as a valid historical promotion before a later interaction.
The promotion must be valid historically and expired at the time of the later request.
The scenario only tests unsupported-information handling when no authoritative answer is available.
An exchange or post-purchase complaint requires an existing purchase.
The persona is explicitly a customer contacting the business for the third time.
Session continuity can only be demonstrated when a later interaction has earlier context to carry forward.
Cross-channel continuity requires customer interactions on more than one channel.
Handoff continuity requires responsibility to move between AI, humans or shifts.
Continuous improvement must compare behavior before and after an approved improvement.
A change-of-mind event needs an original value that can later be superseded.
The generated contradiction must be explicit and measurable.
The generated case should contain information that can be used to evaluate continuity and repeat-question behavior.
Promotion validity must be deterministically known rather than invented by the conversation generator.
Price-comparison conversations need authoritative prices or quotes for consistent generation and evaluation.
The persona definition explicitly states that the customer asks many questions but does not buy.
An individual synthetic case may be a normal case without a difficult-scenario complication.
The PDF requires at least 20 multi-session test scenarios and at least 5 difficult cases for M1.
Persona describes customer behavior, case study describes the system problem, and difficulty adds an optional complication; sampled values must not contradict each other.
